races.name: Racing TV Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Harry's Halo
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but needs the pace to develop; 71 days off is concerning for sharpness in this tactical affair
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown most of his form over 6f on ground softer than good; close third in big field over 5f at Doncaster in sole run this term; enters calculations off same mark back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Surprised
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who showed good form at this course and distance last time; inexperienced apprentice may struggle with tactical positioning
runners_data.comment: Won Beverley novice (7f) as 2yo; promising Catterick run latest; this stiff test can suit
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who has dropped to 6f for last two starts; gradually back to form this season for new stable, close third over C&D (good to soft) most recently; possibilities off same mark.

runners_data.name: Stirrup Cup
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with proven course and distance form; strong trainer/jockey combination gives tactical edge over rivals
runners_data.comment: Twice been unlucky in big-field Thirsk handicaps this spring; enters calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped well and looked rather unlucky in two races at Thirsk in April; two attempts over this C&D (soft) comprise a second-place finish and success; likely player if bouncing back from below-par effort last time.

runners_data.name: Pop Star
runners_data.note: Won over 5f recently so fitness assured; hold-up style needs pace development but good course form provides confidence
runners_data.comment: Reduced mark appeals on form as recent as last September but he's struggled since
runners_data.spotlight: Ended a run of duck eggs with 5f success at Carlisle (good) ten days ago and although back up 5lb he remains well treated on historical data, which includes 6f win off current mark (two years ago); respected.

runners_data.name: Rich Rhythm
runners_data.note: Primarily a 7f performer dropping back in trip; hold-up style faces tactical challenge if pace collapses
runners_data.comment: Always the danger he'll fluff the start; on his last winning mark but comes with risks
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown most of his handicap form over 7f, winning twice on AW; however, both 2026 efforts suggest this return to 6f is worth exploring; effective on turf and he's on a handy mark.

runners_data.name: Too Much
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner gives huge tactical advantage; 49 days off and poor recent form are significant concerns
runners_data.comment: Dual course winner who can miss the break and/or pull hard; didn't offer much on comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Has done her winning on AW but ran well in last two turf attempts; however, brings a doubt over current form, having performed poorly in sole outing this year; upset in stalls and withdrawn last month (28-1 at the time).

runners_data.name: Baba Reza
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 186-day break after wind surgery; freshness unknown and tactical setup unfavourable
runners_data.spotlight: Has had wind surgery on two occasions, namely prior to reappearance success in 2024 (off 3lb higher) and prior to this 2026 seasonal debut; today may prove the time to catch him.

runners_data.name: Coconut Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent style could challenge Too Much early; better over 7f and disappointing recent form limit appeal
runners_data.comment: Three-time course winner who returned to form at Ayr last week; on the shortlist
runners_data.spotlight: Has done most of her winning at 7f; ran respectably in last 6f attempt but was disappointing at Catterick (usually one of her favoured tracks) most recently and needs to rebound.

runners_data.name: Macedonian
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with inconsistent form; tactical setup works against him and recent efforts lack conviction
runners_data.comment: Just 1-15 and inconsistent but on a handy mark and the return to 7f is worth exploring
runners_data.spotlight: AW scorer for previous yard; inconsistent for current stable and has failed to show his form in two starts this term; well treated on best turf efforts but he's not particularly solid.

races.paceDynamic: Too Much is the only confirmed front runner in this field and will dictate proceedings from the start. With minimal early pace pressure, she can control a sustainable tempo through the first half of this 6f contest on soft ground. The majority of the field comprises hold-up horses who will need to come from behind, creating a tactical setup where early positioning becomes crucial. This pace dynamic strongly favours prominent runners and those who can secure good early positions, as the lack of early pace will make it difficult for hold-up horses to close effectively.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Early Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Too Much gets an easy lead with no early challenges
scenarios.body: Too Much sets her own fractions and the hold-up brigade struggle to make up ground on the testing ground. The lack of pace pressure allows her to save energy for a strong finish despite her recent poor form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Coconut Bay or another prominent runner challenges Too Much early
scenarios.body: A genuine pace emerges that stretches the field and sets up the race for closers. The faster early fractions allow the numerous hold-up horses to unleash their finishing kicks effectively.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Positioning Key
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady but positioning becomes crucial turning for home
scenarios.body: Horses that secure good early positions without expending too much energy can capitalize. Those trapped behind the wall of hold-up horses struggle to find racing room in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Surge Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Too Much sets very pedestrian fractions and tires dramatically
scenarios.body: The ultra-slow pace allows the best staying hold-up horses to produce devastating late runs. Fresh legs overcome tactical disadvantages as the early leaders capitulate completely.

watchPoints.text: If Too Much gets away with very slow early fractions, the hold-up horses may struggle to make up ground
Watch for Coconut Bay's early positioning as any challenge to Too Much changes the entire pace dynamic
Stirrup Cup's course form makes him dangerous if he can overcome the tactical disadvantage of his running style
The numerous hold-up horses could create traffic problems in the straight if bunched together
Pop Star's recent 5f winner may have given him the fitness edge needed for this tactical battle

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Capilano
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who should control the tempo but may lack the kick to resist late challenges on this softer surface
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded 72,000gns yearling; inexperience was evident when a rallying third at Newcastle, finishing ahead of Caeruleus; improvement on the cards.

runners_data.name: Light Of Dawn
runners_data.note: Expensive newcomer with unknown style but strong breeding for speed; James Doyle's presence suggests immediate readiness
runners_data.spotlight: Made 140,000gns as a yearling and 625,000euros at a breeze-up sale; half-sister to ten winners including some some smart sprinters, while the dam was a 5f 2yo Listed winner; of major interest for several standout reasons.

runners_data.name: Deputy Vice
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse perfectly suited to the expected pace scenario; Chester third sets a high standard for this grade
runners_data.comment: £145,000 breeze-up 2yo by Mehmas; one of yard's 2yos is 3-3, including in Lily Agnes here
runners_data.spotlight: £145,000 breeze-up 2yo; had a good draw at Chester (6f, good; 11-1) and held his own in what looked a useful novice race; that sets the standard.

runners_data.name: Caeruleus
runners_data.note: Another closer who needs the pace to develop; has 2l to find with Capilano but showed promise when fourth at Newcastle
runners_data.comment: 80,000gns yearling who's only just turned two; the market will be the best guide
runners_data.spotlight: 80,000gns yearling; had only just turned two when fourth at Newcastle 20 days ago; has 2l to find with Capilano but this son of Blue Point was getting the hang of things late on.

races.paceDynamic: Capilano will lead or sit prominent with no other obvious pace pressers in this small field, creating a steady tempo early. Light Of Dawn's running style is unknown but could provide some company if she breaks smartly. The modest pace will set up a sprint finish from the 2f pole where the hold-up horses Deputy Vice and Caeruleus can unleash their kicks. This sustainable pace heavily favours closers who can produce late acceleration in the soft conditions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate as expected and the closers get clear runs
scenarios.body: The soft ground and steady tempo create perfect conditions for Deputy Vice and Caeruleus to produce devastating late runs. Both have shown ability to quicken and will relish the tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Capilano Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Capilano's prominence translates to control and he outstays the closers
scenarios.body: Michael Dods' gelding uses his track position to dictate terms and finds enough in the tank when the closers come hunting. His Newcastle third suggests stamina reserves that could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Light Of Dawn Debuts Impressively
scenarios.trigger: If the expensive Burke newcomer shows immediate class from an unknown style
scenarios.body: Her breeding suggests early pace and the significant investment indicates serious ability that could overwhelm these exposed rivals. James Doyle's booking adds confidence to her chances.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo becomes crawling and turns into a sprint lottery
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure dash where draw and positioning matter more than ability. Any horse getting first run could steal it despite the tactical mismatch.

watchPoints.text: Light Of Dawn's market support will reveal Burke's confidence in this expensive debutante's immediate impact
Capilano's early positioning - if he leads too generously he'll be vulnerable to the closers' finishing kicks
Deputy Vice's ability to secure a clean passage in the straight with McDonald needing to time his challenge perfectly
The actual pace development - if it becomes stronger than expected it could undo the hold-up horses' chances
Caeruleus improving significantly from his debut experience twenty days ago at Newcastle

races.name: Carlisle Racecourse Supporting IJF Beneficiaries Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pearl
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to French 1,000 Guineas/French Oaks winner Avenir Certain; easy to back but showed clear promise with 1l third in novice event at York (1m, good) where she was the sole newcomer (belated debut) in a field of seven; this 4yo filly is the form pick and open to progress to boot.

runners_data.name: Stolen Kisses
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to Italian 1m Flat/2m jumps winner Cult Figure, half-sister to 1m1f winner Givemehoperosa (RPR 73); dam 1m-9.4f scorer (100); pedigree doesn't set the pulse racing; belated debut aged four.

runners_data.name: Midnight Serenade
runners_data.spotlight: Twilight Son half-sister to winners Earn Your Stripes (5f/6f; RPR 59) and Willy Il Coyote (Italian 6.7f-1m); dam 1m4f AW scorer (58); yard not associated with winning newcomers.

runners_data.name: Always Blue
runners_data.comment: Promising second on debut at Ripon but today's tough task may be beyond her
runners_data.spotlight: One of the main form contenders, having finished second at Ripon (1m2f) then just over 1l behind Pearl when 50-1 fifth at York (1m); however, unlikely to reverse placings with that filly, who has bigger potential.

runners_data.name: Foxy Night
runners_data.comment: Pedigree suggests longer trips might suit but yard in good form so worth a market check
runners_data.spotlight: Bred to stay at least 1m; belied her 50-1 odds with fourth of ten, best of the newcomers, in 7f AW contest at Kempton; a possible danger, provided she builds on that effort.

runners_data.name: Marhayb
runners_data.spotlight: Finished 2l fifth of ten in 7f AW event at Newcastle where she started second favourite behind a gelding in the same ownership; recorded an ordinary RPR but may well improve with the experience under her belt.

runners_data.name: Fair Isle Sioux
runners_data.spotlight: 6yo mare who has been absent for over two years since her sole start, namely keeping-on fifth of seven in Redcar contest (6f, soft); likely best watched.

races.name: Watch Racing TV Live Handicap

runners_data.name: Mereside Spark
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning quickly after bleeding incident who may benefit from stronger pace but faces tactical disadvantage
runners_data.comment: Best effort over 5f (soft); below par lately; bled from the nose latest; others preferred.
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race maiden; proved somewhat resurgent with fourth of six upped to 6f at Catterick (good to firm; bled from nose) most recently; may build on that effort.

runners_data.name: Realistic Dream
runners_data.note: Ex-Irish maiden with inconsistent profile whose hold-up style needs more pace than this race will provide
runners_data.comment: Most racing in sprints; not without hope into such a weak handicap down 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden whose lack of consistency has continued for new stable; likely best watched unless the market suggests a big run is expected.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Proven 6f handicapper with good recent form whose hold-up style could benefit from positioning closer in small field
runners_data.comment: Better efforts so far both over 6f; stuck on well when second at Ripon latest; player.
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who ran well at Ripon (good) and Catterick (good to firm) last month, taking her record in 6f handicaps to 322; threatening to win a race of this nature.

runners_data.name: The Cyprus Pearl
runners_data.note: Turf debutante with AW fade tendency whose style offers little hope in likely slowly-run race
runners_data.comment: Huge prices and well beaten in two starts to date; expect more of the same
runners_data.spotlight: Turf/handicap debutante who is far from solid on her AW form; the new scenario needs to make a big difference.

runners_data.name: Auspicious
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up horse proven over course and distance but unraced on soft ground which adds question mark
runners_data.comment: Won at Redcar three weeks ago and just 3lb higher here; strong claims for in-form yard
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on ground softer than good; ran well (neck second) over C&D ten days ago when bidding to follow up his narrow success at Redcar; remains in top form.

runners_data.name: Truly Special
runners_data.note: Only proven front runner returning to sprinting after disappointing longer distance efforts for new yard
runners_data.comment: Didn't offer a lot on her Wetherby comeback for new yard three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who has weak claims on her 1m/7f efforts this term for new yard but, judged on pedigree, may improve for this return to sprinting (second attempt).

runners_data.name: Breeze Star
runners_data.note: Maiden with regression concerns whose wind surgery may improve early pace from 36-day break
runners_data.comment: Offered little thus far, including two sprint nurseries; tongue-tie added for reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Broadly regressive maiden whose chance depends on the effects of physical tweak (wind surgery since last run).

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Garden
runners_data.note: Long-absent AW specialist whose hold-up style and venue change represent significant unknowns
runners_data.spotlight: Has recorded RPRs in the 30s on Newcastle AW; change of venue/surface needs to prompt a good deal of improvement.

runners_data.name: Charcon
runners_data.note: Another AW specialist returning after 114 days whose sole turf attempt was disappointing
runners_data.comment: Poor form so far and first-time visor needs to spark improvement back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Far from solid on form mostly shown on Newcastle AW; failed to beat a rival in seller in sole turf attempt (debut).

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: Improving 6f handicapper whose recent form suggests she can compete despite poor trainer strike rate
runners_data.comment: 66-1 winner at Newcastle in October; needs to back it up now returned to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Improved form since racing in 6f handicaps, recording 66-1 win on AW last autumn then 33-1 second at Catterick (good) on reappearance; may well remain competitive.

runners_data.name: Independent Angel
runners_data.note: Fading hold-up runner with two recent zeros whose poor form trend continues negative trajectory
runners_data.comment: Unable to get competitive in any of her five handicaps and she's hard to fancy
runners_data.spotlight: Has achieved little in terms of form and two duck eggs this season highlight her poor chance.

races.paceDynamic: Truly Special is the only confirmed front runner in this field and should dictate terms from the start without serious early pressure. Breeze Star may provide some company in the early stages but lacks the consistent pace-pressing profile to create a strong gallop. The moderate early tempo will allow the large contingent of hold-up horses to stay in touch before the real racing begins in the final two furlongs. This pace setup clearly favors horses with tactical speed and finishing kick over those needing a strong gallop to show their best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Truly Special gets an easy lead and dictates soft fractions
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows the front runner to kick clear when ready while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on the testing ground. Truly Special's proven stamina at longer trips gives her the edge in a slowly-run sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace sets up perfectly for closers with tactical speed
scenarios.body: Horses like Auspicious and Battenburg Belle can position closer than usual and use their proven 6f form to strike late. The soft ground aids their stamina while hindering pure speed horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Truly Special fails to fire and no other horse takes up the running
scenarios.body: The race becomes a crawl with bunched horses turning for home, favoring any horse with a turn of foot regardless of recent form. Long-absent runners like Charcon could benefit from the tactical nature.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Speed Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Breeze Star's wind surgery has transformed her early pace and she can press Truly Special
scenarios.body: A genuine tempo emerges that stretches the field and allows horses with proven early speed to hold on. The testing ground becomes less of a factor when horses are committed early.

watchPoints.text: Truly Special must be monitored for early position as the only natural leader in a pace-deficient field
Auspicious faces first test on ground softer than good which could expose stamina limitations despite recent good form
Breeze Star's early pace after wind surgery could determine whether any genuine tempo develops
Multiple hold-up runners including Battenburg Belle and Lanarra may struggle if positioned too far back in slowly-run race
Market support for long-absent Charcon would signal stable confidence after venue and surface change

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing TV Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Epidavros
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces traffic concerns but has won over course and distance on soft ground, though mounting losing run suggests stagnation
runners_data.comment: C&D scorer; in decent nick, fourth at Musselburgh latest; 2lb out of handicap though
runners_data.spotlight: Losing run is mounting up and her three fourth placings this season reflect stagnation, rather than building towards a win; that said, she has won over C&D (soft) and returns here off a workable mark.

runners_data.name: Ravishing Beauty
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose solid 2023 form has deteriorated, needs revival to be competitive from awkward tactical position
runners_data.comment: Won two in a row at about 1m (good) last summer; soundly beaten on return from a break
runners_data.spotlight: Solid spell of form last term featured two wins and three second-place finishes; has gone rather off the boil since but a revival would give her good claims off current mark.

runners_data.name: Positive Thoughts
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner besides the leader, ideal tactical position but form has declined since handicap debut disappointment
runners_data.comment: Maiden; makes handicap debut; best efforts have been on AW; first run on fast ground
runners_data.spotlight: Has gone rather backwards since a good autumn effort on AW, disappointing favourite on handicap debut (7f) most recently; chance depends on the effects of new trip and first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: We've Got This
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but poor overall record and slight form dip makes her vulnerable in traffic
runners_data.comment: Consistent last season; made low-key return but might be boosted by new cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Record is only 1-13 and her form has dipped a touch in two outings this term; normally a consistent sort otherwise and, as per many times, has frame possibilities if back on song.

runners_data.name: Blufferonthebus
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with excellent Carlisle record including two wins, recent frame finishes suggest return to form
runners_data.comment: Hinted at revival with Beverley sixth latest, finishing well; very much one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: In reasonably good form, having made the frame twice last month, third at Catterick latest; dual winner at Carlisle (soft/good to firm) and returns to this venue off a favourable mark; respected.

runners_data.name: Angela's Baar
runners_data.note: Five-race maiden showing late headway over 1m last time, hold-up style faces usual traffic concerns with this field makeup
runners_data.comment: Below-par fifth at Wolverhampton in February; switch to h'caps needs to spark progress
runners_data.spotlight: Five-race maiden who has failed to build on debut promise; however, made some late headway upped to 1m last time and there may yet be a bigger effort in her in handicaps.

runners_data.name: Emery Down
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner improving for new yard but 0-11 handicap record and need for clear run poses problems
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark but her best form has come on AW and others hold stronger claims
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 0-11 in handicaps since AW maiden win; however, steadily heading back in the right direction for new yard, fourth at Yarmouth (1m) most recently; possibilities off reduced mark.

runners_data.name: Rosemary May
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with concerning finishing kick issues and poor handicap form since maiden win
runners_data.comment: Last of ten on her return at Ripon (1m) 26 days ago; hood is reached for now
runners_data.spotlight: Far from convincing on her handicap form since winning Ayr maiden in April 2025; best watched unless the betting suggests a turnaround is likely.

runners_data.name: Music Academy
runners_data.note: Sole front runner faces first-time turf exposure but uncontested lead opportunity with Ralph Beckett's 7/34 strike rate
runners_data.comment: Big step forward with Kempton third last month; can do better still so needs considering
runners_data.spotlight: Thrice-raced filly who posted best effort when third at Kempton (AW) on penultimate start; may be capable of progress now handicapping, provided she takes to first-time headgear; shortlisted.

races.paceDynamic: Music Academy is the lone confirmed front runner and will dictate proceedings uncontested from the gate. With eight hold-up horses and only Positive Thoughts showing prominent tendencies, the pace will be sustainable rather than testing. Music Academy can control fractions through steady sectionals, creating a tactical race where positioning becomes crucial in the straight. This setup strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the large pack of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Scores
scenarios.trigger: If Music Academy gets an easy lead and maintains steady fractions
scenarios.body: The Ralph Beckett filly controls the race from pillar to post, while the massed ranks of hold-up horses struggle for racing room in a bunched finish. Front running tactics prove decisive on this tight track with a large field of similar ability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Traffic Jam
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes crawling and the field remains tightly bunched turning for home
scenarios.body: Eight hold-up horses create a wall of traffic as they all come with their runs simultaneously, leading to interference and blocked passages. Only those with the clearest runs or rails positions can capitalize from this large contingent.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts can track Music Academy and outstay her in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The Jason Hart-ridden filly uses her prominent style to sit second throughout before challenging the tiring leader. Her tactical position proves crucial as the hold-up brigade encounters the predicted traffic problems behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Specialist
scenarios.trigger: If the good to soft conditions significantly favor horses with proven soft form
scenarios.body: Blufferonthebus's dual Carlisle wins and superior soft ground record (2W3P from 15 runs) becomes the deciding factor. Her track experience and going preference override the tactical disadvantage of racing from behind.

watchPoints.text: Music Academy must handle the turf surface switch as her three previous runs were on all-weather tracks
Traffic congestion is inevitable with eight hold-up horses in a nine-runner field on Carlisle's tight circuit
Positive Thoughts represents the only tactical alternative to sitting behind Music Academy's uncontested lead
Blufferonthebus has strong Carlisle form but Craig Lidster's 0/10 recent record raises trainer form concerns
The good to soft going report consistency suggests conditions will play fair across all runners

races.name: Follow Racing TV On X Handicap

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor recent form but good historical Ripon record, needs significant improvement off long break
runners_data.comment: Closely matched with Classic Encounter on 2025 York form, but not at best last few runs.
runners_data.spotlight: Gained most recent success off 3lb higher last July, enhancing his good record at Ripon; not in anything like the same form since; difficult to support with confidence.

runners_data.name: King Of Fury
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who races too freely sometimes, good second-place record suggests he's competitive at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Triple AW winner who failed to get home, having raced too freely, over 1m2f in that sphere last time (still ran respectably); 0-12 on turf but was a good second off 6lb higher in last attempt; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Style Of Life
runners_data.comment: Has a broadly progressive record on turf for current yard; remains of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Record for current stable includes periods of progression at up to 8.5f; seemed to need the run at York on seasonal debut but she'll need to leave the bare form of that duck egg well behind.

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid Carlisle form including track win, needs to step forward from recent moderate efforts
runners_data.comment: 3-39 overall, last winning in August 2024, and he's probably best watched first time out
runners_data.spotlight: Form at Carlisle features a success in 2024 and close second last June, both off much higher marks; a possible danger provided he takes a sufficient step forward from Beverley reappearance duck egg.

runners_data.name: Sound Janet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from wind surgery, stable debut was poor but operation may have resolved issues
runners_data.comment: Expensive to follow for Roger Varian before sold for 25,000gns; market useful
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up a few times for previous yard; folded tamely and finished last on stable/seasonal debut but her subsequent wind surgery may prompt a better effort.

runners_data.name: Concert Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who excels at Newcastle AW but struggles on turf, difficult task returning to grass after 73 days
runners_data.comment: All five wins have come here and he's been in good heart here of late; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Does most of his racing at Newcastle (AW) where he has registered all five wins; generally consistent this year but seems to have a difficult task back on turf, being 8lb higher than last attempt.

runners_data.name: Skinny Malinka
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 591-day absence including failed hurdles debut, market will be telling
runners_data.comment: 0-7 under rules but made the frame four times for Ed Bethell in 2024.
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since pulled up in December 2024 when making hurdles/stable debut; consistent six-race maiden on Flat for previous yard; market instructive.

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: Front-runner with excellent recent form including C&D win, best to forgive stumbling start last time
runners_data.comment: Easily made all Carlisle on Friday; 6lb higher today but still a leading candidate
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive since November, particularly on good ground this spring; gained most recent win over C&D; best to forgive latest effort (stumbled start, unable to adopt usual front-running tactics); remains of interest.

runners_data.name: Redarna
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran with prolific winning record including at Carlisle, drop in grade may revive fortunes
runners_data.comment: Nine-time course winner but he's struggled at Musselburgh and Thirsk this year
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who has been a prolific winner down the years, including at Carlisle; not solid on 2026 form but this drop back in grade may have positive effect; successful in last Class 5 attempt.

runners_data.name: Pink Azalea
runners_data.note: Front-runner with perfect Carlisle record (1-1) but form has been dismal recently, track specialist angle
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo filly whose handicap record is split into two halves, namely a progressive one followed by a dismal one; however, 1-1 at this track and could revive if her favoured soft ground materialises.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose form has dipped this season including poor C&D effort last time
runners_data.comment: Poor strike-rate but may have needed reappearance run and he's on a competitive mark
runners_data.spotlight: Made the frame in most starts last term for new yard but form has dipped in two outings this term, latest over C&D; doesn't look as if he's about to belatedly add to his Irish 2yo win.

runners_data.name: Star Cast
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good progressive form with four wins this year, effective over longer trips
runners_data.comment: Having a good year and chasing a quick hat-trick; stamina for 1m4f still to be proven
runners_data.spotlight: Generally progressive on AW/turf this year, winning four times over 1m2f; creditable third over 1m4f at Musselburgh last time; remains in form and may still have more to offer at this level; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid record for current stable, creditable Newbury third on seasonal return
runners_data.comment: E-w player if in same form as 12 months ago (won this race); this time it's after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Has a record of 3-7 (Flat/hurdles) for current yard; creditable third at Newbury (1m4f, good) on seasonal debut most recently; major player off same mark, assuming he copes with this drop back in trip (stiff track and forecast slow ground are helpful in that respect).

runners_data.name: Titainium
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 322 days with preference for good to firm ground, soft going concern
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since a dismal effort on soft ground last July and again has a doubt over the forecast surface; has gained both turf wins on good to firm.

races.paceDynamic: Krissy, Pink Azalea and the notable absence of Style Of Life (non-runner) leaves two confirmed front-runners to set the tempo over this 1m1f trip. King Of Fury and Runninsonofagun will likely sit prominently behind the leaders, creating a sustained gallop that will test stamina on the soft ground. The pace will be honest rather than frantic, with the real action starting from the 3f pole as the hold-up horses try to pick off the pace-setters. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can position prominently and kick when it matters, rather than pure hold-up merchants who may find too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not destructive
scenarios.body: The prominent racers get first run on the leaders and have enough left to repel late challengers on ground that saps finishing kicks. Horses like King Of Fury and Amancio benefit from the perfect tactical position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Hold Sway
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy and Pink Azalea dictate without serious pressure
scenarios.body: The front-runners control the tempo completely and kick clear when the pressure comes, with their fitness and course form proving decisive. Krissy's recent C&D win and Pink Azalea's track record become crucial factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or becomes stop-start
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect scenario with a tactical race that becomes a sprint finish, allowing their superior class to emerge. The soft ground aids their stamina reserves in a slowly-run contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast early and crack
scenarios.body: Krissy and Pink Azalea burn each other out in a speed duel, creating opportunities for patient types with proven stamina. The 1m1f trip becomes crucial as horses need to stay the distance strongly.

watchPoints.text: Krissy's early position will be crucial given her front-running style and recent stumbling start issues
Pink Azalea's early pace-setting could either revive her Carlisle magic or expose her recent poor form
Sound Janet's wind surgery recovery will be evident in how she travels through the race
King Of Fury's tendency to race too freely could undermine his chances over this staying trip
The market support for long-absent Skinny Malinka will indicate stable confidence after hurdles experiment

runners_data.name: Rwenearlytheredad
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with proven course form who benefits from wind surgery and suitable soft conditions
runners_data.spotlight: Had wind surgery prior to Ayr reappearance effort that seemed to be needed; gained most recent success off 4lb higher over C&D (good to soft) just over a year ago and looks interesting back here.

runners_data.name: Tarlac
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping up in trip which should help inconsistent sprinter on reduced mark
runners_data.comment: Sole win came over C&D but not obviously in good enough form to capitalise on falling mark
runners_data.spotlight: Campaigned mostly over 6f; inconsistent since sole win; his chance of taking advantage of a reduced mark partly depends on the effects of this return to 7f; record over this trip isn't fully conclusive.

runners_data.name: Pallas Lord
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader whose turf form is poor but gets uncontested advantage with weak pace competition
runners_data.comment: 1-1 here and a close third at Hamilton last time, but fast ground probably not ideal
runners_data.spotlight: Has recorded the majority of his wins on Newcastle AW; below par over C&D ten days ago, failing to build on his Hamilton effort; still hasn't scored on turf since 2022.

runners_data.name: Orbital Chime
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 33-day break and new connections after poor spring form with previous trainer
runners_data.comment: Couple of expensive defeats lately; capable off this mark but strike-rate doesn't inspire
runners_data.spotlight: Poor strike-rate; eventually lost his form during spring spell with James Owen and was sold for 2,200gns since last run; best watched unless the market suggests a revival is likely.

runners_data.name: Jkr Cobbler
runners_data.note: Closer who ran well at course previously but disappointed last time at Hamilton 20 days ago
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner who hasn't been running badly this year without the breaks; on handy mark
runners_data.spotlight: Has gained most wins at Ayr/Newcastle but he defied a higher mark over C&D two years ago; basically running okay this year until never dangerous last time; has the ability to take a serious hand.

runners_data.name: Ideal Guest
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner 10lb below last winning mark who showed promise on Catterick reappearance 18 days back
runners_data.comment: 5-40; ended last season on a downbeat note and no win since October 2023; monitor only.
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 0-13 for current stable but he remains 10lb below last winning mark and holds a good chance provided he builds on Catterick reappearance effort (finished third).

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling this term for new yard despite winning off higher mark last season
runners_data.comment: Sole success came over C&D from 4lb higher last August, but regressive since
runners_data.spotlight: Far from convincing on his efforts this term for new yard, latest back at Carlisle, but looks a plausible danger provided he revives; defied a 7lb higher mark over C&D last August (sole win).

runners_data.name: Albeyours
runners_data.note: Low-mileage closer in cheekpieces who ran well on seasonal debut at Doncaster on similar ground
runners_data.comment: Won at Leicester last autumn and she still has low mileage; needs a close look on return
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 5yo who has form figures of 1253 since wearing cheekpieces, most recently third in big field at Doncaster (7f, good to soft) on seasonal debut; solid claims in the retained headgear.

runners_data.name: Dolly's Delight
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose sole win came on fast ground creating doubts about soft surface
runners_data.comment: Some work to do with Saisons d'Or from Southwell (fifth); the task isn't impossible.
runners_data.spotlight: Registered sole success on fast ground; has rather inconsistent form for current yard; brings doubts over the forecast surface and whether she'll be in top form.

runners_data.name: Baby Rover
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose recent efforts suggest she needs this 7f trip more than previous shorter distances
runners_data.comment: Of interest on 2025 best; should be at concert pitch after two runs back
runners_data.spotlight: Registered sole win over 6f but recent efforts suggest she may need further now and she is less exposed over 7f than shorter; otherwise needs to step up on 2026 bare figures.

races.paceDynamic: Pallas Lord is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the start, likely getting an uncontested lead on the soft ground which should suit his hold-up style better than expected. Tarlac and Dolly's Delight may track him prominently but neither is aggressive enough to apply serious early pressure. The moderate pace will allow the large contingent of hold-up horses (Rwenearlytheredad, Orbital Chime, Jkr Cobbler, Ideal Guest, Sir David, Albeyours, Baby Rover) to stay in touch throughout. This sustainable gallop heavily favours closers who can unleash their finishing kicks in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Pallas Lord sets his usual moderate tempo without serious early challenges
scenarios.body: The soft ground and steady pace creates perfect conditions for the multiple hold-up horses to deliver their runs simultaneously. Rwenearlytheredad and Albeyours benefit most from the combination of their proven course form and finishing style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If Pallas Lord gets completely uncontested fractions and the field settles too far back
scenarios.body: Despite his poor recent turf form, the veteran gets first run on horses that leave it too late to respond. His experience at getting soft leads allows him to repel late challenges on ground that may not suit his usual pace style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Tarlac or Dolly's Delight track closer than usual and quicken approaching the final furlong
scenarios.body: The step up to 7f helps both horses who have been campaigned too short recently. Their forward positions give them first jump on the deeper-held horses when the sprint develops.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the entire field goes to sleep behind Pallas Lord through ultra-slow early sectionals
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the three-furlong pole favouring horses with natural pace regardless of usual style. This chaotic finish opens the door for any horse in good current form.

watchPoints.text: Pallas Lord could steal this if he gets completely uncontested fractions and the field settles too passively behind
Albeyours has strong recent Doncaster form and proven soft ground ability but trainer is 0/8 recent runners
Rwenearlytheredad showed course form and wind surgery benefit but hasn't won for over a year
Tarlac stepping up in trip could unlock improvement after inconsistent 6f campaigns
Multiple hold-up horses may get in each other's way if they all produce runs simultaneously in final quarter-mile
